title: NICE CG151 Neutropenic sepsis: prevention and management in people with cancer
sections: NICE CG151 asks clinicians to suspect neutropenic sepsis in anyone who becomes unwell during or after anticancer treatment, to treat it as an acute medical emergency, and to start empirical antibiotic therapy immediately without waiting for the neutrophil count. Patients receiving chemotherapy should be told how to contact a 24 hour advice line and to seek help urgently if they develop a fever or feel unwell.

title: NICE NG234 Spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression
sections: NICE NG234 covers the recognition and management of spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression in adults with cancer. New back or neck pain with neurological symptoms such as limb weakness, sensory change or bladder or bowel dysfunction in a person with cancer should prompt immediate contact with the metastatic spinal cord compression coordinator or acute oncology service and urgent MRI of the whole spine, so that treatment can start before function is lost. NICE NG122 refers to NG234 for the management of spinal metastases in lung cancer.
